hypothesis: A valid scope-111 DTS can be obtained by replacing the first row of the published scope-112 witness with a multi-mark perturbation within radius 10 while keeping the other six rows fixed.
rationale: Single-mark local search cannot resolve the five conflicts introduced by the clamped 112; a deterministic multi-mark neighborhood can test the same structural vicinity exhaustively and identify whether the obstruction is confined to one row.
expected_information_gain: Either produces a scope-111 witness or exhausts a defined neighborhood, quantifying how far the published first row is from compatibility with the other six rows.
method: Enumerate the first row recursively with each of its five marks within +/-10 of the published values, enforce increasing marks, row-internal difference uniqueness, and disjointness from the six fixed rows. Validate any complete row using the independent DTS verifier.
metric: complete compatible first-row replacements and maximum searched row difference count
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete replacement accepted by the independent validator is an exact scope-111 DTS; exhaustive failure within the radius is a localized negative result, not a global impossibility proof.
kill_condition: Stop at the first independently validated target witness or after 60 seconds; preserve whether the defined neighborhood was exhausted.

raw_result.instrumentation_note: The first implementation only updated its partial-score counter on complete rows; no partial-score claim is made.

interpretation: The radius-10 neighborhood around the published first row contains no complete row compatible with the other six fixed rows at scope 111. The search exhausted the defined neighborhood without reaching the target; this is localized negative evidence only.
what_was_learned: The five conflicts caused by clamping cannot be resolved by changing all five first-row marks within +/-10 while leaving the other six rows fixed.
recommended_next_action: Generalize to reversible multi-row exact-cover/backtracking search; do not broaden this one-row neighborhood repeatedly without a new hypothesis.
